text:
Aisha: Flagging a weird short-tail multilang regression on the new embed candidate 'heron-lite-v3' in staging. Recall@3 on ja/ko short queries dropped ~9% vs prod.
Tom: Oof. Which slices exactly? raw numbers?
Aisha: Ran a 4k query sweep across en, ja, ko, es. Short queries (<6 tokens) per-lang recall@3: en 0.72->0.73 (ok), ja 0.61->0.52, ko 0.59->0.50, es 0.70->0.69.
Ravi: Are these translation-near-duplicates leaking? Our cross-lang dedupe is loose. I can run fuzzy-translate-dedupe and rerun.
Tom: Also check norming: heron-lite-v3 switched to L2-normalize post-quant. Could be numeric drift for short vectors. Show silhouette/entropy?
Aisha: silhouette (cosine): en 0.44, ja 0.31, ko 0.29. cluster entropy per-lang higher for ja/ko (0.82 vs 0.61 en).
ops-bot: eval-job started 4898765432-multilang-scan on staging.
Ravi: Reran with stricter dedupe (translate-hash threshold 0.85). Short-query recall@3 improved a bit: ja 0.54, ko 0.52. Not enough.
Tom: Hypothesis: quantization + embedding norming + small tokenizer differences in ja/ko lead to embedding collapse for short tokens. Let's try: 1) per-language calibration shards 2) contrastive negatives augmented with back-translations 3) PCA-whitening postproc.
Aisha: Good plan. Start with per-lang calib (512 batches each) + keep fp16 for baseline. Then int8-calib per-lang.
Tom: Command for baseline run:
```./run_eval.sh --model heron-lite-v3 --set shards=per_lang_calib:512 --dataset multilang-shorttail --metrics recall@1,3,10,silhouette,entropy --norm l2```
Ravi: Also adding backtranslation negatives generator to the data pipeline: `bt-gen --langs ja,ko --n 2` so short queries get synthetic hard negatives.
Aisha: FP16 + per-lang-calib results: ja recall@3 0.58, ko 0.56, silhouette ja 0.35, ko 0.33, entropy ja 0.68. Still ~4% lower than prod but improved.
Tom: int8 per-channel PTQ without per-lang calib gave ja 0.50. With per-lang int8-calib it matches fp16-ish: ja 0.57, ko 0.55. PCA-whitening on top gives small bump ja 0.59.
Ravi: Backtranslation negatives helped precision@1 for short ja queries (0.46 -> 0.51) but recall@3 gains modest. Hard negatives seem to separate near-translation clusters.
Aisha: Perf tradeoffs? int8-calib median latency down 2.6x vs fp16. PCA adds tiny 3% overhead in runtime.
Tom: Risk profile: small remaining gap vs prod on ja/ko (~1-2% recall@3). Can we add perturbation test (token-drop, half-char) to daily smoke and watch short-tail specifically?
Aisha: Yes. Proposal: canary onboard heron-lite-v3 int8-calib + PCA at 3% traffic limited to non-critical routes, monitor recall@3 per-lang with alert if drop >1.0% over baseline for 15m. Also add silhouette floor: ja/ko silhouette <0.32 => rollback.
Ravi: I'll author the rollout spec and add backtranslation negatives to the nightly create-maintenance dataset.
ops-bot: rollout-config created 4898765432-canary (3%) with rollback hooks.
Tom: One more check: try hybrid-quantization (fp16 first 3 layers) — might stabilize short token semantics. If hybrid beats int8-calib by >0.5% on ja/ko recall@3, prefer that for canary.
Aisha: I'll schedule a hybrid run and post results here. Thanks all, great triage. :rocket:
